messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 — Elevated 401/403 responses from RedisCloud auth proxy observed across multiple hosts. Errors causing cache GETs to fail and triggering fallback to rate-limiter strict mode. Paging eng-sre + eng-runtime. Pager: https://pagerduty.example/incident/2345
Sara (on-call): Ack. I'm looking at dashboards now. Which services are seeing the highest 429/500 spike?
Ken (eng-runtime): Mostly embedding and streaming routes that depend on cached user tokens. Rate limiter is seeing a surge because cache miss -> upstream auth call -> 401 -> we treat as deny.
Maya (eng-sre): Logs show auth proxy returning intermittent 401s starting ~11:58 UTC. Circuit-breaker is tripping on our cache client when auth calls fail.
Alice (eng-platform): From trace sampling: requests to rediscloud-auth.example.net return 401 with body "invalid token" for ~20% of calls, but from other regions it's fine. Could be a token rotation bug on their side.
Ken (eng-runtime): Quick mitigation idea: treat 401 from auth-proxy as “soft fail” if we have a local cached value (stale-ok for 30s) and avoid flipping rate limiter to hard-block. Can we toggle that?
Maya (eng-sre): We can flip `CACHE_STRICT_AUTH=false` via config toggle in console, but need to be careful for security-sensitive routes. Suggest scoped bypass for non-critical routes.
Sara (on-call): Start mitigation: 1) Enable local read-through fallback (stale-while-revalidate) for 5 minutes. 2) Increase auth retry backoff to reduce hammering. 3) Bypass strict rate-limit for dedicated-customer routes for now. Who can execute?
Alice (eng-platform): I can push the feature flag for fallback to 30s stale. Will do a canary on 10% of traffic first. Command: `./deployctl flag set CACHE_SWR=30s --canary=10%`
deploy-bot: deploy queued by Alice. CI checks passed. Rolling canary to 10% (3 hosts) now.
Ken (eng-runtime): Adding conservative client-side retry: `CACHE_FETCH_RETRIES=4`, `CACHE_FETCH_BACKOFF_MS=400` in runtime config. Deploying patch to avoid immediate deny on single auth failure.
Maya (eng-sre): Pasted error excerpt from app logs:
```
2026-03-15T11:59:03Z ERROR cache_client.go:142 getKey failed err="auth proxy 401: token invalid" host=rediscloud-auth.example.net
2026-03-15T11:59:03Z WARN rate_limiter.go:78 increment blocked reason="auth-fail"
```
Ken (eng-runtime): Also seeing connection resets when auth proxy returns early 403. That causes our client to mark host unhealthy and failover which adds latency and more auth attempts.
Maya (eng-sre): Escalating to RedisCloud support — opening a joint investigation. Ben, can you open a customer-facing incident note?
Ben (support): Drafting now. Proposed message: "We’re investigating an external cache authentication issue affecting token validation for some requests which may cause increased errors or rate limiting. We have temporary mitigations in place and are working with our cache provider. We will update within 30 minutes." Shall I post to status.redwood.example?
Sara (on-call): Yes, post to status (not yet tweeted). Include known affected endpoints: /v1/embeddings, /v1/generate-stream. Mark as partial degradation for EU/US-west.
Ben (support): Posted: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/RC-2026-03-15-1 :thumbsup:
RedisCloud Support: Thanks for the report. We see a token refresh regression in the auth proxy cluster tied to a config rollout at 11:50 UTC. Eng on our side investigating. We'll share root cause ASAP.
Maya (eng-sre): Now the runbook steps. 1) Canary SWR (Alice) ✅ 2) Increase retries/backoff (Ken) ✅ 3) Temporarily relax rate-limiter policy for critical customers — I propose policy patch: `rate_limit.strict_for_unknown=false` for embedding routes. 4) Add a short-lived override to force local LRU for 60s on hosts with >10% auth errors.
Ken (eng-runtime): Patching rate limiter config (will scope to service: embeddings). Config snippet: `RATE_LIMIT_OVERRIDES=[{"service":"embeddings","strict_for_unknown":false}]` — applying now to canary then global if green.
deploy-bot: Rate limiter config update rolled to canary (3 hosts). Monitoring for 5m.
Sara (on-call): Handoff note: I'm stepping out in 30m. Handoff to Maya for next shift. Maya, you own next updates and communication with RedisCloud.
Maya (eng-sre): I have the handoff. I'll coordinate with RedisCloud and keep status updates every 15 minutes. Taking primary incident slack.
Ken (eng-runtime): Observability notes — adding a temporary metric `cache_auth_error_rate` and dashboard panel. Please watch for decrease after canary.
Alice (eng-platform): Canary metrics show 10% reduction in immediate 429s for canary hosts. No obvious increase in erroneous data returns. Rolling to 30% now.
Ben (support): Customer impact triage: - Large enterprise customers on Dedicated: minimal (we skipped strict rate-limits). - Self-serve free tier: increased 429s for ~12% of requests in EU region. Will prepare targeted email to affected customers if this persists.
RedisCloud Support: We identified a bad token rotation job; rolling back the 11:50 UTC deploy should restore normal behavior within 5-10 minutes. We'll perform rollback now.
Maya (eng-sre): Great. Once they rollback, we should revert our temporary relaxations carefully. Plan: wait 10m post-rollback, then remove SWR flag and restore rate-limiter strictness in staged fashion.
deploy-bot: RedisCloud reports rollback complete. External alerts showing auth 401s dropping.
Ken (eng-runtime): Seeing auth errors drop to baseline across regions. Reverting our overrides:
- `CACHE_SWR` -> disabled (remove flag)
- `RATE_LIMIT_OVERRIDES` -> remove embedding override
- `CACHE_FETCH_RETRIES` -> set back to normal
Alice (eng-platform): Reverting flags with canary first. `./deployctl flag remove CACHE_SWR --canary=10%`
deploy-bot: Canary revert complete. Proceeding to global revert.
Sara (on-call): Back from break. Thanks team. Any customer escalations?
Ben (support): No high-severity escalations yet. Sent follow-up note to customers explaining root cause and mitigation timeline.
Maya (eng-sre): Post-incident tasks: 1) Add explicit handling for auth-proxy 401s to avoid immediate rate-limit block. 2) Add automated detection to flip to SWR only for transient auth spikes (less than 5m). 3) Run tabletop with RedisCloud to prevent bad token-rotation deploys.
Ken (eng-runtime): I’ll open the runtime PR to treat single auth failures as soft-fail and add histogram metrics for auth error latency.
Ben (support): Draft postmortem section for customer-facing status: cause, mitigation, timeline, next-steps. I'll tag legal for wording.
Maya (eng-sre): Closing notes: incident downgraded to monitoring at 12:45 UTC. I'll remain the owner until 15:00 UTC. If auth-401 rate creeps above 1% again, re-open P0.
Oncall Rotation: Handoff acknowledged. Great run. :clap:
Sara (on-call): Closing thread. Thanks everyone.
